aliases: Positron Annihilation into Dark Matter Experiment

facility_roles.quote: The PADME experiment (Positron Annihilation into Dark Matter Experiment) at Laboratori Nazionali di Frascati of INFN aims to search for a “Dark Photon” using positron on target collision at the DAΦNE Beam Test Facility.

intervals.label: proposal
intervals.note: Start = the arXiv date (8 January 2015) of the earliest description fetched; the date of the proposal itself is not given. End = INFN's approval at the end of 2015.
intervals.quote: The PADME experiment proposes a search for the dark photon (A0 ) in the e+ e− → γA0 process in a positron-on-target experiment, exploiting the positron beam of the DAΦNE linac at the Laboratori Nazionali di Frascati, INFN.

intervals.label: approved by INFN; design and construction
intervals.note: Start 'the end of 2015'. End: the page says the collaboration 'completed the design and the construction of the experimental apparatus in mid 2018' (year precision here).
intervals.quote: At the end of 2015 INFN has formally approved a new experiment, PADME, to search for invisible decays of the A' at the DAΦNE Linac in Frascati.

intervals.label: commissioning
intervals.locator: Bertelli et al. (arXiv:2305.08684), abstract; end from arXiv:2205.03430
intervals.note: Start = switching on in 2018 (the home page expected data from October 2018 to February 2019). End = July 2019, when data with a primary positron beam 'represented the completion of the commissioning of the experiment' (arXiv:2205.03430).
intervals.quote: Since switching on in 2018 the experiment has collected more than 1013 positrons on target (PoT)

intervals.label: data taking at the DAΦNE Beam Test Facility
intervals.note: Start = the end of commissioning (July 2019). INFN's page describes the experiment in the present tense; the latest data-taking campaign found is Run III (October to December 2022) and no end is stated.
intervals.quote: The PADME experiment explores the existence of a fifth force mediated by the so-called dark photon and connected with dark matter.

intervals.label: Run II
intervals.note: Second half of 2020; 430 MeV positrons, about 5.5 × 10^12 positrons on target (arXiv:2603.28685); dark-photon search data.
intervals.quote: The PADME Run II data taking was realized in the second half of 2020.

intervals.label: Run III (X17 resonance scan)
intervals.note: Positron beam energy scanned between 262 and 296 MeV (√s from 16.4 to 17.4 MeV) in a three-month data-taking period.
intervals.quote: Run III, which took place from October to December 2022

website.quote: The PADME experiment (Positron Annihilation into Dark Matter Experiment) at Laboratori Nazionali di Frascati of INFN aims to search for a “Dark Photon” using positron on target collision at the DAΦNE Beam Test Facility.

name: PADME
notes: PADME uses the positron beam of the DAΦNE linac at the Beam Test Facility (BTF-1), not the DAΦNE collider rings; accelerator:dafne is listed because INFN describes the BTF as part of the DAΦNE complex and no separate linac record exists.
Kind fixed_target: a positron-on-fixed-target experiment (the 2022 paper calls it 'a fixed target experiment exploiting a positron beam').

physics_goals.quote: The experiment is designed to detect dark photon produced in positron on fixed target annihilation (e+e−→γ A) decaying to dark matter by measuring the final state missing mass.
physics_goals.value: Search for a dark photon A' produced in e+e- → γA' with a pulsed positron beam on a thin target (missing-mass technique), later also a resonant scan for a 17 MeV boson (X17)

summary.plain: An experiment at Frascati's Beam Test Facility that sends pulsed positrons from the DAΦNE linac into a thin diamond target to look for a dark photon, and in 2022 scanned the beam energy for a hypothetical 17 MeV particle, the X17. It has set new limits.
summary.technical: PADME: bunched e⁺ beam from the DAΦNE linac and BTF-1 (up to about 550 MeV), 20×20 mm² active polycrystalline diamond target in vacuum, 0.5 T dipole with charged-particle vetoes, 616-crystal BGO electromagnetic calorimeter, small-angle calorimeter and TimePix3 beam monitor; e⁺e⁻ → γA' by missing mass at √s of 14 to 23 MeV. INFN approval end 2015, commissioning to July 2019, Run II 2020, Run III October to December 2022 (X17 scan, 262 to 296 MeV); JHEP 11 (2025) 007: limits, largest deviation about 2σ global at √s ≈ 16.90 MeV.
